proposed.explanation:
COMI (CIB Egypt) shows strong fundamental growth that aligns with your high-growth, 10-year horizon profile. Key evidence: (1) Net loans grew ~48% YoY (343.5B → 508.0B EGP), (2) customer deposits grew ~14% (972.6B → 1,110.4B EGP), (3) net interest income rose ~18% (91.1B → 107.7B EGP), and (4) basic EPS increased ~24% (14.72 → 18.25 EGP). These are encouraging signals of a bank expanding its franchise and earning power.

However, important caveats: (a) we only have one year of comparative data, so we cannot confirm a sustained growth trend; (b) loan growth (48%) far outpaces deposit growth (14%), suggesting aggressive balance-sheet expansion that could carry credit risk; (c) no data on NPL ratios, capital adequacy, or profitability margins is available; (d) this is a single stock, so your portfolio will be concentrated in one bank.

Given your high risk tolerance, long horizon, and no liquidity needs, a position in a growing bank is reasonable. I recommend buying 58 shares at 128 EGP (cost 7,424 EGP), leaving 7,576 EGP in cash. This keeps COMI at ~49.5% of your 15,000 EGP portfolio, respecting the 50% single-position limit. The remaining cash preserves optionality to add to the position or diversify into other names as more evidence becomes available.

Risks: Egyptian banking sector is sensitive to interest-rate policy, inflation, and currency movements. A 48% loan expansion in one year may not be sustainable and could lead to credit-quality deterioration. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.

COMI net loans and advances to customers at Dec 31, 2024: 343,542,674,000 EGP (343,542,674 × 1,000)
COMI due to customers (deposits) at Dec 31, 2025: 1,110,395,693,000 EGP (1,110,395,693 × 1,000)
COMI due to customers (deposits) at Dec 31, 2024: 972,595,958,000 EGP (972,595,958 × 1,000)
COMI net interest income for FY2025: 107,699,631,000 EGP (107,699,631 × 1,000)
COMI net interest income for FY2024: 91,064,222,000 EGP (91,064,222 × 1,000)
COMI basic EPS for FY2025: 18.25 EGP per share (per-share metric; the page-level 'thousands' unit does not apply to EPS)
COMI basic EPS for FY2024: 14.72 EGP per share (per-share metric; the page-level 'thousands' unit does not apply to EPS)

limitations: Only one year of comparative financial data is available (FY2025 vs FY2024); no multi-year trend can be assessed.
No information on non-performing loan ratios, capital adequacy ratios, or cost-to-income ratio is provided.
The 48% loan growth vs 14% deposit growth gap raises questions about funding sustainability and potential credit risk, but no NPL data is available to assess this.
No dividend information, share count, or market capitalisation data is provided to assess valuation.

The EPS unit on the page is stated as 'EGP thousands' but is interpreted as EGP per share, as is standard for per-share metrics; if the thousands unit were applied literally, the figure would be implausible.
